intro: What changed, in the order it changed, for the people using it rather than the person who wrote it. Versions are commits — see the badge in the sidebar for the one you are on.

sections.heading: Accounts, and sharing the archive
changes: **Invitations.** Accounts are created by invitation. There is no email service, so an invitation is a link the administrator sends you directly. It works once and expires in a fortnight.
**Two-factor authentication**, optional for ordinary accounts and required for administrators. You are shown ten recovery codes once; write them down.
**Password reset without email.** The administrator issues a one-time code and reads it out; you choose your own new password. They never learn it.
**Storage limits.** Your account page shows what you have used. An upload that would take you past the limit is refused before the file is stored, and the message says the numbers.

**An administrator cannot read your documents.** They administer accounts, storage and the pipeline. There is no view-as and no override — the permission boundary has no administrator branch, and a test asserts it on every route that returns data.

sections.heading: Signing in
changes: **Bindery's own login page** replaces the Cloudflare Access screen that used to sit in front of it. One account, one password, one page.
Repeated wrong passwords are slowed down and eventually locked out for a quarter of an hour. A successful sign-in clears it, and an administrator can clear it sooner.

sections.heading: Guides and versions
changes: **Guides** for every screen, and answers to the questions people actually ask, at *Guides* in the sidebar. Served from this machine; no part of it needs a network.
**The version** of what is running is in the corner of the sidebar, with a warning when the pieces disagree or a database migration has not been applied.

sections.heading: Finding things
changes: **Photos** — every image in the archive as a wall of pictures rather than a list of filenames, with a filter for the ones nothing could be read from. Bindery can look at those and describe them.

**Folder tidying.** *Organise* proposes which folders, document types and tags are the same thing under different names. Only the names are sent for this — never any document text — and nothing merges until you agree to a group.
